standard.title: Many-to-one data displays
standard.description: Acquire data for categorical and discrete numerical variables to address a question of interest or purpose, using digital tools; represent data using many-to-one pictographs, column graphs and other displays or visualisations; interpret and discuss the information that has been created
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can collect categorical and discrete numerical data and record using frequency tables (AC9M3ST01). They have not yet used many-to-one displays where one symbol represents multiple data points.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students acquire data, represent it using many-to-one displays, and interpret and discuss the information shown.

nodes.label: Many-to-one representation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain and interpret many-to-one pictographs and column graphs where one symbol or unit represents more than one data point.
nodes.minimum_width: Interpret one many-to-one pictograph; identify the key value (what one symbol represents); answer one question about the data.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret many-to-one pictographs and column graphs, including reading the key value, answering questions and identifying the most/least common categories; explain why reading the key before making judgements is essential; distinguish many-to-one from one-to-one displays.
wider: Investigate how digital platforms generate word clouds, quizzes and graphical summaries from collected poll data — connecting data representation to real AI-powered tools
Compare many-to-one representations with different key values for the same data set, discussing how the choice of scale affects readability and impression

response_modes.reason: Students who only work with one-to-one displays may misread many-to-one displays by counting symbols without applying the key. Encountering multiple displays with different key values — including poorly chosen scales — develops the habit of reading the key first.

nodes.hinge_reason: Students who do not apply the key when reading many-to-one displays will systematically misinterpret data in Node 3 — constructing displays with an inappropriate key value, or interpreting their own display by counting units rather than applying the scale. The key-first habit must be in place before construction.
success_criteria: Students can read the key of a many-to-one display and use it to accurately interpret the data
Students can explain what one symbol or column unit represents in a given display

nodes.label: Acquire and record data
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can acquire data for a question of interest using appropriate methods and record using digital tools.
nodes.minimum_width: Collect data for one question using observation or a simple survey; record in a tally chart or digital table.
nodes.typical_width: Acquire data through surveys, observations, experiments and repeated chance trials; record using tally charts, digital tables and spreadsheets; use digital tools for data organisation; collect data across categorical and discrete numerical variables.
wider: Use secondary data about fire burns to construct data displays that assist First Nations Ranger Groups and other groups to care for Country/Place
Co-create an online poll and explore how the platform generates graphical summaries of the responses, comparing the automated display with a student-made column graph of the same data
success_criteria: Students can collect data for a question of interest and record it in an organised format
Students can identify whether their variable is categorical or discrete numerical

nodes.label: Construct and interpret displays
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can construct a many-to-one display and interpret and discuss the information it reveals.
nodes.minimum_width: Construct one many-to-one column graph or pictograph from collected data using a digital tool; identify and discuss one feature of the data.
nodes.typical_width: Construct many-to-one pictographs and column graphs using digital tools; interpret displays by describing the distribution and identifying patterns; discuss what the data shows in relation to the original question; make at least one inference beyond the immediate data.
wider: Construct displays of science experiment data and interpret them in terms of the scientific investigation — connecting statistics to cross-curriculum science inquiry
Acquire and graph data from repeated chance experiments, comparing column graphs across multiple trials and connecting the statistical variation to probability concepts

response_modes.reason: Constructing and interpreting a data display is an integration task — students coordinate data collection, representation decisions, key value choices, and interpretation simultaneously. The quality of the interpretation reveals whether the full statistical inquiry cycle is understood.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Many-to-one displays in real contexts — including science experiments, chance investigations, and community data — give statistics a genuine purpose and connect data representation to authentic questions.
success_criteria: Students can construct a many-to-one display using a digital tool, including an appropriate key
Students can interpret their display by identifying and discussing at least two features of the data
